chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said:

"When you enter the mosque, say: 'In the name of Allah, and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah. Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and peace be upon them, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. O Lord, forgive my sins and open for me the doors of Your grace.' And when you leave, say the same."

key_terms.مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Muhammad and the family of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for entering and leaving the mosque in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith outlines the etiquette of entering and exiting the mosque, emphasizing the intercession of the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt as a means to access divine grace. The supplication reflects the Shia emphasis on *tawassul* through the Prophet's family, linking physical entry into the sacred space with spiritual purification and the opening of Allah's doors of favor.
